about: Needs of the food consumption model (R64, M112), version 2. Every value is copied from research/economy/nutrition_record.md (section 2i: four levels; 2j: recommended intake, athletes, upper limit, toxic and lethal doses; 2a-2f: energy, water, absorption, gut limits). Levels: minimum = lowest intake keeping deficiency signs absent or balance kept; mean = what a population eats (not a target); optimum = intake where a marker levels off; ceiling = lowest intake with observed harm in people, in daily intake units. A value is a number or [low, high]. Basis says how a level scales: per_day; per_kg (body weight); per_1000_kcal (energy turnover); per_g_protein (protein eaten); absorbed (amount taken up, before dividing by absorption).
model_constraint_rule: Only availability, the energy need, the user's ceilings per good (milk 3 L, 250 g fat from one good, fruit at most one watermelon; M86, M88, M93) and lactose for people neither lactase persistent nor a dairy culture constrain eating. Protein counts as energy up to the liver's daily urea capacity (a rate, spread over three meals). The nutrient ceilings, the protein ceiling of 2-2.5 g/kg or 35 % of energy and fat are harms, reported, never constraints (M101, M114). Starvation is read from the minima: energy of basal function (1.2 x REE) and every nutrient minimum (M114).
model_target_rule: The adequacy target of a nutrient is its optimum; where the record finds no plateau (potassium, magnesium) it is the recommended intake of section 2j. The deficiency threshold is the minimum. The ceiling is the observed-harm level; where the observed harm is not in daily intake units (iodine) the upper limit of section 2j is used, named as such.

ree_kcal.source: Mifflin et al. 1990, PMID 2305711: weight-only equation REE = 15.1 W + 371 (R2 0.56); the full equation with height, age and sex is 9.99 W + 6.25 H - 4.92 A + 166 S - 161

pal_limits.source: Black 1996 (1.2-4.5); Westerterp 2001 (2.2-2.5); Thurber 2019 (food intake limits supply at about 2.5 x basal rate; beyond it body stores are drawn down)

caffeine.source: Dulloo et al. 1989, PMID 2912010: 100 mg every 2 h over 12 h, +150 kcal a day in lean adults

turnover_ml.source: Yamada et al. 2022, PMID 36423296, PMC9764345: WT (ml/d) = sum of coefficient x variable; sex 1 male 0 female; HDI group 0 high, 1 middle, 2 low; explains 47.1 % of the variation

metabolic_water_ml.source: Tipton, Exp Physiol 2025 (review): about 0.5 L a day at rest

minimum_drink_l.source: Tipton 2025: about 1 L to drink at rest in mild conditions; urine at least about 0.5 L

renal_ceiling_l_per_h.source: Noakes et al. 2001, PMID 11732457: peak urine 778 ml/h; excretion above about 900 ml/h not possible

hydration_index.source: Maughan et al. 2016, PMID 26702122: water retained 2 h after 1 L relative to still water; tea, coffee, lager, juice not different from water (1.0)

intake_limit.source: Bilsborough and Mann 2006 (record 2e): theoretical safe maximum 285-365 g a day for 80 kg, set by the liver's capacity to make urea; per kg = 285/80 to 365/80. A daily rate, spread over three meals (M114); protein up to it counts fully as energy

gut_absorption_g_per_h.source: Bilsborough and Mann 2006: the gut absorbs 1.3-10 g amino acids an hour

as_energy.source: Excess protein is used for energy (Bilsborough and Mann 2006: requirement levels ignore the use of protein for energy metabolism; M114: excess protein is turned into glucose); 4 kcal per g as in the composition records

gut_limits.lactose_context: The limit comes from studies of pasteurised milk or lactose in water in lactase-deficient people; it does not apply to lactase-persistent people or dairy cultures (M113). Live-culture yogurt: 18 g lactose gave about one third of the breath hydrogen of the same lactose in milk (Kolars et al. 1984, NEJM 310:1); pasteurisation destroys the lactase of the cultures.

whole_animal.about: Goods eaten as the whole animal (M91, M113): composition built from part records by part shares. Atwater factors 4/9/4 kcal per g protein/fat/carbohydrate recompute energy where only the fat changes.

cod_as_eaten.source: Torry Advisory Note 17 (FAO 2001) part shares; the coastal meal moelje is cod, cod liver, fresh cod-liver oil and roe (Skjervoy, northern Norway; Public Health Nutrition 2004, Brustad et al.); liver record: lingcod liver (USDA 169810, 42 % fat); vitamin A of the liver from cod liver oil (USDA 173577) times the liver fat share

herring_whole_fat_pct.source: Faroese and Atlanto-Scandian herring measured with head and intestines, 1950s (Frodskaparrit, ojs.setur.fo, article 275): lowest in May, highest about 1 August

cod_liver_lipid_farmed.source: farmed cod on high-lipid feeds: liver lipid 719-785 g/kg, 83-88 % of body lipid (Stirling study); not used: farmed, not wild

cod_head_viscera.source: Bechtel 2003 (pollock and cod processing by-products); not used: no record that heads and viscera were eaten as food

alcohol_g_per_week.source: Wood et al. 2018, PMID 29676281; GBD 2018, PMID 30146330
